items.text: Report on Recent San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Activities, Events and Announcements Dennis Herrera, SFPUC General Manager, announced that former SFPUC Commissioner, Francis “FX” Crowley, who had also served on the San Francisco Civil Service Commission, the Port Commission, as a labor leader, a great community leader and as husband to SFPUC Press Secretary Nancy Crowley, passed away; and, SFPUC FEBRUARY 25, 2025 MEETING MINUTES Page 2 of 8 Mr. Herrera stated that he would like to adjourn this meeting in honor of Francis Crowley. Commissioner Arce provided comment relating to community impacts from the work performed on local and hyperlocal hiring and contracting, contributing it to the effort and pursuit of a first in the nation mandatory local hiring policy and strategy by former City Attorney and current SFPUC General Manager Dennis Herrera

items.title: Bay Area Water Supply and Conservation Agency Report
CONSENT CALENDAR

Approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. PRO.0169, Project Pull Citywide Internship with Japanese Community Youth Council, increasing the contract duration by two years by exercising the first of two 2-year options to extend under the contract, to continue providing San Francisco youth with summer internship opportunities among City departments, for a total duration of six years, with no change to the contract amount
items.decision: approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 7a and 7c

items.title: Award Contract No. WW-727, Various Locations Sewer Replacement No. 16, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Precision Engineering, Inc., in the amount of $8,702,449 and with a duration of 580 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year and seven months) to replace/line existing sewers on specified streets in the City and County of San Francisco. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action. (Not applicable)
items.decision: approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 7a and 7c

items.title: Award Contract No. PRO.0289, As-Needed River Ecosystem Science Services, to Applied River Sciences, for an amount not to exceed $4,000,000 and with a duration of eight years, to provide the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Natural Resources and Lands Management Division professional services to support river ecosystem science and management efforts. Item 7b was not considered by the Commission
items.decision: approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 7a and 7c

items.title: Approve the form of a Revolving Credit Agreement with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association in the total principal amount of $200 million
items.text: Approve (1) the form of a Revolving Credit Agreement with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association (Wells Fargo) in the total principal amount of $200 million and (2) the related Fee Agreement, pursuant to which agreements a principal amount of not-to- exceed $100 million at any one time will support the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Water Interim Funding Program and a principal amount of not-to-exceed $100 million at any one time will support the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Power Interim Funding Program, separately; and authorize the General Manager to enter into the same agreements with Wells Fargo. [Water Enterprise ][Power Enterprise ]

items.title: Approve the expansion of the California Water Service Company Bear Gulch District service area; and approve the 4th Amendment to the Individual Water Sales Contract between the CCSF and Cal Water
items.text: Approve the expansion of the California Water Service Company (Cal Water) Bear Gulch District service area due to the City of Menlo Park’s transfer to Cal Water of the service obligation for the County of San Mateo’s Flood Park; and approve the Fourth Amendment to the Individual Water Sales Contract between the City and County of San Francisco (San Francisco) and Cal Water, to adjust the boundaries of the service area where Cal Water may use or sell water delivered by San Francisco, in accordance with section 3.03.E of the 2021 Amended and Restated Water Supply Agreement

items.title: Approve Amendments No. 1 to Contract Nos. PRO.0231.A-D, Specialized and Technical As-Needed Services, with Stantec/JHCE Joint Venture
items.text: Approve Amendments No. 1 to Contract Nos. PRO.0231.A-D, Specialized and Technical As-Needed Services, with Stantec/JHCE Joint Venture (JV) (PRO.0231.A), MMD JV (PRO.0231.B), AECOM/WRE JV (PRO.0231.C), and Lee Incorporated (PRO.0231.D), increasing each contract amount by $5,500,000 to address the higher than anticipated contract usage rate, due to an increased need for consulting resources with highly specialized skillsets, as well as an increased need for significant changes to infrastructure and asset management practices, and environmental and regulatory requirements, for a new total not-to-exceed contract amount of $13,000,000 for each contract, with no increase to the contract duration, subject to the Board of Supervisors approval pursuant to Charter Section 9.118

items.title: Adopt a refined Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act and award Contract No. WD-2909, Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant Short Term Improvements
items.text: Adopt a refined Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act and award Contract No. WD-2909, Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant Short Term Improvements, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Western Water Constructors, Inc., in the amount of $44,938,784, and with a duration of 1,258 consecutive calendar days (approximately three years and five months), for the repair of sediment and flocculant basin concrete; replacement of sludge removal equipment, channel and filter valves, cationic polymer system, and sample pumps; and installation of chemical piping. In addition, a new utility water pump station will be installed to support the facility

items.title: Approve an increase of 365 calendar days to the duration contingency for Cathodic Protection for Transmission Pipelines at Various Locations, Phase 2, with EXARO Technologies Corporation
items.text: Approve an increase of 365 calendar days to the duration contingency for Contract No. WD-2845, Cathodic Protection for Transmission Pipelines at Various Locations, Phase 2, with EXARO Technologies Corporation, for a revised duration limit of 1,168 consecutive calendar days (approximately three years and three months), with no change to contract amount, to provide additional time to complete remaining contract work due to Pacific Gas and Electric Company delays in providing utility power service

items.title: Approve an increase of the cost and duration contingency of $2M and 350 calendar days, for Channel Force Main Intertie, with Anvil Builders, Inc.
items.text: Approve an increase of $2,000,000 to the cost contingency and an increase of 350 calendar days to the duration contingency, for Contract No. WW-723R, Channel Force Main Intertie, with Anvil Builders, Inc., for a revised contract amount limit of $19,375,899 and a revised contract duration limit of 1,131 consecutive calendar days (approximately three years and one month), to address extensive dewatering needed due to unforeseen site conditions, and extend dry weather restricted work into 2025 to support ongoing shoring and dewatering activities

items.title: Approve Amendments No. 1 to Agreement Nos. PRO.0275.A-C, Hetchy Capital Improvement Projects As-Needed Construction Management and Staff Augmentation Services
items.text: Approve Amendments No. 1 to Agreement Nos. PRO.0275.A-C, Hetchy Capital Improvement Projects As-Needed Construction Management and Staff Augmentation Services, with AECOM and Effective Management Services LLC. Joint Venture (PRO.0275.A), Avila and Associates Consulting Engineers, Inc. (PRO.0275.B), and Hetchy CM Partners Joint Venture (PRO.0275.C), to provide as-needed construction management services to augment City construction management staff as necessary, increasing each agreement by $2,000,000, for a total not-to-exceed amount of $6,000,000 (per contract), with no change to the contract durations, to continue critical support services for ongoing public work projects
